clue.text: Made to become an owner

parts.note: reads like being turned into a proprietor, but describes the act of buying, the deal that makes someone the owner

explanation.surface: Someone finds they have been turned into a proprietor.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying something is the transaction that makes you its owner.

clue.text: Forgot to mention charity, in the Bible?

parts.note: PS, postscript, is added for something you forgot to mention
alms are charity given to the poor

explanation.surface: Someone forgot to mention charity, wondering if it's in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of the Old Testament made up of sacred songs.

clue.text: Arrangement for tabour played with freedom

indicators.note: a musical arrangement for the drum, so its letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A drum part is arranged to be performed loosely.
explanation.walkthrough: A tabour is a small drum played with a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical direction for flexible tempo, where the performer speeds up and slows down expressively.

clue.text: Wounded fish plunging

parts.note: wounded means hurt
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An injured fish dives downwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Rushing headlong or crashing violently downwards.

clue.text: Bird was injured by pole

indicators.note: injured means damaged, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: N is the north pole

explanation.surface: A bird was hurt by a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-necked water bird.

clue.text: In these hills chaps get duck

parts.note: chaps are men
to duck is to dip, as under water

explanation.surface: Out walking in the hills, the lads go for a plunge.
explanation.walkthrough: The MENDIPS are a range of limestone hills in Somerset, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper name of a range of limestone hills in Somerset.

clue.text: Clad ceremonially, is borne upwards from earth

definitions.note: the definition is a past form; the answer is the verb, to dress ceremonially

indicators.note: in a down entry, upwards means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for earth, in electrics

explanation.surface: Someone in ceremonial dress is carried up from the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upwards' fits a down entry: the word is read bottom to top, giving ENROB. 'Clad' is a past form while the answer is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on robes or vestments, as for a ritual.

clue.text: Read eagerly -victory for us in action!

indicators.note: the letters for victory and for us go in the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an action
V is victory, as in V for Victory
our means belonging to us

explanation.surface: A war-time cry of victory for us, read eagerly from a news report.
explanation.definitionFit: To devour a book is to read it greedily, as if eating it.

clue.text: Big ears on little ones, we are warned

definitions.text: Big ears on little ones, we are warned

parts.words: Big ears on little ones, we are warned
parts.note: the proverb that little jugs have big ears, warning that children overhear adult talk

explanation.surface: A warning that small children have big ears.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'little pitchers have big ears' warns that children overhear; a pitcher's handles are its ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Jugs whose handles are called ears, the subject of the proverb about eavesdropping children.

clue.text: Polar bear heading off, for a change, to be living in trees

indicators.note: the remaining letters are changed around into a new order
the head of the first word comes off, so its first letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A polar bear, away from the ice for once, takes up life in the treetops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops the P of Polar; 'for a change' rearranges OLAR BEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Arboreal describes animals that dwell among branches, as monkeys and sloths do.

clue.text: Pot-holder? That's right!

parts.note: a stand for a hot pot, and the old saying 'as right as' this three-legged stand, meaning perfectly sound

explanation.surface: A quiz host confirms a contestant's guess about a pot-holder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As right as a trivet' is an old British saying meaning in perfect order.
explanation.definitionFit: A trivet is a three-legged iron stand for a pot or kettle, and proverbially stands for soundness.

clue.text: Opera made to run smoothly if given a boost

indicators.note: boosting pushes upwards, so in a down entry the pieces are read from the bottom

parts.note: an engine made to run smoothly has been oiled
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stage show runs smoothly if it gets a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given a boost' reverses OILED IF as a whole to give FI DELIO; this is Beethoven's only opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's only opera, about a wife rescuing her imprisoned husband.

clue.text: You'll find me lost in such accommodation

indicators.note: you'll find the letters of the two words in a new arrangement, so they are to be mixed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone warns they get lost in roadside lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder: ME and LOST together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Motels are roadside lodgings for motorists, a kind of accommodation.

clue.text: Top's missing from bristly toilet accessory — it's to smooth out the wrinkles

indicators.note: the top, the first letter, of the item described is missing

parts.note: a bristly item for one's toilet (grooming) is a hairbrush

explanation.surface: A hairbrush has lost its top, though it promises to iron out wrinkles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toilet' here is the old sense of grooming and dressing, not the lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: To retouch a photograph with a fine paint spray, removing blemishes such as lines in the face.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing husband

definitions.meaning: to husband resources is to economise, consuming fewer of them

explanation.walkthrough: 'husband' as a verb means to manage thriftily; read as two words, the answer says just that.
explanation.definitionFit: Of no value or purpose; and, split in two, an instruction to economise.

clue.text: Dance a short distance

definitions.meaning: a quick ballroom dance in two-four time from the early twentieth century
a single pace, a very small distance

explanation.definitionFit: Both a brisk 1910s ballroom dance and a single pace, the shortest of distances.

clue.text: The main river, or burn

parts.note: the main is a poetic name for the open sea

explanation.surface: A choice between the ocean, a river, or getting scorched.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorch or char a surface with intense heat.

clue.text: In hot water for illicit hunting?.

definitions.meaning: cooking eggs or fish gently in simmering liquid
taking game or fish from someone's land without permission

explanation.walkthrough: 'In hot water' looks like being in trouble, but means a cooking method.
explanation.definitionFit: Both gently cooking in simmering water and catching game unlawfully on another's land.

clue.text: A loaming process and this tree blossoms

indicators.note: to process material is to work it over, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Spreading loam over the ground makes a tree burst into blossom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'process' reworks LOAMING into MAGNOLI, with A set at the end; 'blossoms' completes the picture of the tree in flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree or shrub famed for its large waxy flowers.

clue.text: Suspicious about youth becoming cleaner

indicators.note: the word for suspicious goes about, around, the word for youth

parts.note: chary means wary or suspicious
a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A wary person is suspicious about a young man who becomes a cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: A charlady is a British term for a woman hired to clean houses or offices.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired domestic cleaning woman, a char.

clue.text: Half-hearted backing for the alternative, so it's said

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Half-hearted backing for the alternative, so it's said' (4) for ORAL. 'so it's said' defines ORAL and OR is 'the alternative', but no reading of 'Half-hearted backing' gives AL; possibly an OCR or setter slip, unconfirmed.
annotationWithheld.clue: Half-hearted backing for the alternative, so it's said

clue.text: It's deceiving to the eye and a little to the ear

indicators.note: to the ear means as heard, so the word for the next phrase is what you hear

parts.note: slight means small, a little

explanation.surface: Something fools the eye, and says a little to the ear too.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits in 'deceiving to the eye', as in sleight of hand, a conjuror's deft trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight is dexterous trickery, as in a conjuror's sleight of hand that fools onlookers.

clue.text: Recent mix-up concerning the heart

indicators.note: a mix-up jumbles things, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A recent mix-up concerning a heart problem.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle or core of something is its heart.

clue.text: A bad thing to part company with this enterprise?

indicators.note: parting the letters for company, the other letters go between them

parts.note: a sin is a bad thing

explanation.surface: A gambler loses money at a gaming business and wishes to quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part company' looks like one phrase, but 'company' is CO, parted by A SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambling house is a business, an enterprise where people bet on games of chance.

clue.text: Help out, and get medal for coolness

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: GM is the George Medal, a British gallantry award

explanation.surface: Lending a hand earns someone a medal for staying calm.
explanation.walkthrough: The George Medal (GM) is a British award for bravery by civilians.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm composure, an unflappable temperament; one of the four humours.

clue.text: Study poetry? Just the opposite!

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Someone suggests reading poetry and gets told it's the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: The converse of a statement is its opposite or reverse.

clue.text: Hint at this also being crack

definitions.meaning: to raise a subject tentatively, bring it up for discussion
to pierce or open a cask or bottle, as one cracks open a drink

explanation.definitionFit: To bring a topic up for talk, and to pierce a cask to draw its liquor.

clue.text: Drive a point home?

parts.note: reads as making an argument stick, but literally describes hammering a pointed metal pin into wood

explanation.surface: A speaker insists on hammering their argument home.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointed metal spike driven in with a hammer.

clue.text: Sounds of the silent sort

indicators.note: of the silent sort means made of the letters of the word sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: Noises that make no noise at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds' looks like noises, but means narrow sea channels, as in Puget Sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow arms of the sea, such as straits or creeks, are both inlets and sounds.

clue.text: March is held in limbo

indicators.note: the word is is held inside the word for march

parts.note: a march is a parade
taken as written

explanation.surface: The month of March is stuck in a state of uncertainty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month, but is a procession. Limbo here is the abode of the righteous dead before Christ, sometimes called Paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: In Christian tradition the waiting place of the righteous dead, Abraham's bosom, is also called by this name.

clue.text: Kitchen utensil it's not so small, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, so the word for not so small is heard

parts.note: something bigger, not so small, is greater

explanation.surface: Someone reports that a kitchen gadget is larger than they thought.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheese shredder with a rough perforated surface is a standard kitchen tool.

clue.text: Othello, perhaps, with lead character returning for fun and games here

parts.note: Othello is an example of a play, by Shakespeare

indicators.note: returning means the word for the lead character is read backwards

parts.note: the lead character in Othello is the Moor

explanation.surface: A theatre staging Othello turns into a place for fun and games.
explanation.walkthrough: Othello does double duty in the surface only: it is a play, and its title role is the Moor.
explanation.definitionFit: A room set aside for children's games and toys.
